# Media generated by artificial intelligence

[Version française](NOTICE-MEDIA.fr.md)

Some media handed out with Lucium were not drawn, filmed or composed by a person: they were generated by artificial intelligence. This page says which ones, where they come from, and what license they have: none. It is a statement of the maintainer, not a legal opinion.

## Which media

| Media | Where | Handed out |
|---|---|---|
| Nine background videos and their nine posters | `resources/backgrounds/lucium-*.mp4` and `lucium-*.jpg` | In this repository and in the application (the "Videos of Lucium" of a space's background) |
| The music of the presentation film | Not in this repository, not in the application | With the film, on [lucium.app](https://lucium.app) |

## Where they come from

- **The videos** were generated on 6 November 2026 with the online service Higgsfield, under the maintainer's paid subscription: a still picture (the model GPT Image 2.6), then its animation (the model MiniMax H3 or Wan 3.0, video by video). The project then resized three of them, blended the loop over one second, encoded them and took the posters, with ffmpeg. The table of the models and the settings is in [`resources/backgrounds/README.md`](resources/backgrounds/README.md) (in French).
- **The music of the film** was generated with Higgsfield too. The maintainer says so; the repository holds neither the file nor a record of the date and the model.
- The prompts given to the service and the files as the service returned them are not in the repository.

## Their license: none

- These media are **not under the GPL-3.0-or-later** of the code, **not under a Creative Commons license**, and not under any other free license.
- The maintainer hands them out with Lucium on the strength of the terms of the service, read in their version dated 23 October 2026. The terms of each model behind the service were not read.
- **This project grants no license on these media and promises no right to reuse them.** Whether you may copy, change or hand them out, apart from passing on Lucium as it is, depends on the terms of the service and of its models and on the law of your country. This page does not settle it.
- Two things those terms forbid, as the maintainer read them: using these media to train a model, and removing the provenance signals of a generated file.

If you hand out a modified version of Lucium and do not want to depend on this, remove the eighteen files from `resources/backgrounds/` and their entries from `src/shared/builtin-backgrounds.ts`, the list the application reads.

## Provenance marks

The files of `resources/backgrounds/` are kept as they entered the repository on 6 November 2026. They are not encoded again, so that whatever mark of provenance they carry stays in them. What was read in them on 11 November 2026: no provenance record in the container (no C2PA manifest), and the tag of the encoder, ffmpeg. A mark hidden in the picture itself cannot be read from here. Do not strip or re-encode these files to remove such a mark.
